h2: Is SNT-TC-1A changing? ASNT's modernization project and what employers should do now
html:
Is SNT-TC-1A changing? ASNT's modernization project and what employers should do now

ASNT is running a multi-year project to modernize SNT-TC-1A, and people searching for the latest edition increasingly ask whether the requirements on this page are about to change. The short answer from ASNT's own project page (last updated August 2026) is that there is no immediate change: employers should keep following the edition of SNT-TC-1A their written practice names, and ASNT has said it will publish transition guidance and effective dates well before any new requirement applies.

What ASNT says the project is about

  • Clearer terminology and roles, and requirements that are easier to find and apply.
  • Guidance, templates and education for the Responsible Level III and for program administrators.
  • A shift toward demonstrated performance in qualification, with training and experience kept as the foundation.
  • Clearer expectations for oversight of employer programs.

ASNT describes four phases (listening and research, a framework and resources, communication and preparation, then transition and support) and says the first is under way. It has not decided whether the Level I, II and III structure will change, or whether training and experience hours will be replaced. It also states that personnel qualified under current practices remain qualified, and that the project is not a conversion of SNT-TC-1A into ISO 9712.

What an employer can do in the meantime

Nothing in the project changes today's obligations, but two habits will make any transition easier. First, keep the written practice current with the edition it cites and record why each requirement is set the way it is; ASNT expects employers may eventually need to update parts of their written practices. Second, keep good evidence of practical performance: practical examination records, the specimens used and the results. Performance is where ASNT says qualification is heading.

If your written practice needs a review, our outsourced ASNT Level III consulting covers written practices, examinations and audits. Technicians working toward certification can start with NDT Level 1 training or NDT Level 2 training, practise in the Practical NDT simulator, and test themselves with the free practice tests.
